objective: Count file entries recursively in a bounded immutable folder tree.

relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Nested application data often needs counts without mutation.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Base cases and branch sums transfer to other tree queries.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: One accumulator and recursive child calls fit the stated tier.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Duplicate names and frozen input expose incorrect counting and ownership.

defects: Tree shape, depth, ownership and duplicate-name policies were implicit.
Deduplicating names and removing children passed prior cases.
rationale: Specify an acyclic ordinary tree of at most 1000 distinct entries and height 100, with absent children for files and dense arrays for folders. Count entries regardless of equal names. Add frozen duplicate names, a hundred-entry chain and a 999-file root. All revealed forms and a reducer alternative agree; prior destructive/deduplicating variants fail. The O(n) cost includes folders and empty folders, not only files.

objective: Track changes with exact strict inequality and independent closure state.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Strict comparison and closures are current JavaScript semantics.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Remembering the immediately previous value is a practical event-state pattern.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Identity versus contents transfers to caches and UI state.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: A flag and previous value fit the closure tier.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: NaN, signed zero and opaque references prevent incorrect comparison policies.

defects: Strict equality was named but its NaN, zero and object implications were not demonstrated.
Object.is and serialization comparisons passed all prior cases.
rationale: Make the existing !== contract explicit rather than changing it. Add repeated NaN, signed zeros, identical-looking/mutated objects, symbols, functions, BigInts and a thousand repeated opaque inputs with a throwing getter. State bounded-value unit-comparison cost and constant stored history. Preserve all reveals, including the private inaccessible Symbol sentinel. Both wrong comparison policies now fail.

objective: Maintain an independent Number running total and count without rounding or history scans.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Closure state and arithmetic averages remain current.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Incremental aggregation is useful for counters and streaming summaries.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Constant-state updates transfer to other online calculations.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Two variables and one update function fit the foundation level.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Explicit floating-point policy and long history prevent misleading decimal and lifecycle claims.

defects: Input/call bounds and decimal arithmetic policy were unspecified.
Rounding averages and stopping after ten calls passed the short existing fixtures.
rationale: Specify at most 1000 finite bounded Number inputs, a total initialized to zero, ordered addition and no rounding. Add a repeating fractional mean, a thousand updates and independent interleaved signed/fractional values. Preserve all reference forms and a function-declaration alternative. The O(1) target is per update under Number arithmetic, not a statement that all updates together take constant time.

objective: Cache the first exact result while forwarding all first-call arguments within a stated callback contract.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Function wrapping and closures remain current.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Avoiding repeated initialization and preserving result identity are practical.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Arguments, identity and independent state transfer to other wrappers.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: The existing tier-three closure exercise fits the explicit nonthrowing callback domain.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Cache-value and argument-count tests prevent silently altered results.

defects: Argument count/reference forwarding and result identity were untested.
Exception, reentrant and dynamic-this behavior was unspecified and revealed forms differed outside a simple callback domain.
Cloning cached objects and forwarding only two arguments passed old cases.
A positional-sounding first-answer phrase was replaced with cached-value wording.
rationale: Define a synchronous nonthrowing bounded-cost callback independent of dynamic this and not reentrant, with at most eight arguments and 1000 calls. Explicitly leave exception/reentry policies outside this exercise instead of claiming a production-general once helper. Add exact object/function/symbol and falsy result caching, full eight-argument count/reference forwarding, empty args and repeated calls. All three supplied forms pass, while cloning and truncated-argument wrappers fail. O(1) excludes unbounded callback/argument work through explicit bounds.
